sentences.text: Wuttagoonaspis was a primitive arthrodire placoderm fish that lived in Australia during the Middle Devonian.
The animal had a box-like skull measuring up to 18 centimeters in length and a median dorsal plate averaging 10 centimeters.
The type species Wuttagoonaspis fletcheri was described by Ritchie in 1973.
The species Wuttagoonaspis milligani was described by Young and Goujet in 2003.
Wuttagoonaspis belongs to the family Wuttagoonaspidae and is closely related to the genus Yiminaspis.
Fossils of Wuttagoonaspis date from the Pragian to the Eifelian stages, between 413.02 and 387.95 million years ago.
